```{r setup, include=FALSE}

```

## Background

Ozone readings came from the Roosevelt Island monitor, using the `airquality` data.

## Monthly ozone

Mean ozone for each month, leaving out days with no reading.

```{r monthly-ozone}
monthly_ozone <- aggregate(Ozone ~ Month, data = airquality, FUN = mean)
knitr::kable(monthly_ozone, digits = 1)
```

## Next steps

Ask the borough office for the 1974 readings.

reference.answer: I added the Monthly ozone section between Background and Next steps. Its table gives mean ozone by month from airquality and leaves out days with missing readings.

turns.user: my rmd runs fine when i do the chunks by hand in the session but knitting it fails, can you fix it? and tell me why it worked in my chunks but not on knit. dont want to loose the area calcuation

required: Knitting runs in a clean R session, so packages and objects from the live session are not available to it.
The chunk that reads and transforms the data has to run before the chunk that uses it.

steps.document:
---
title: "NC county areas"
output: html_document
---

```{r read}
library(sf)
nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
nc_albers <- st_transform(nc, 5070)
```

```{r area}
nc_albers$area_km2 <- as.numeric(st_area(nc_albers)) / 1e6
head(nc_albers[, c("NAME", "area_km2")])
```

reference.answer: The document is fixed. Knitting runs in a clean R session, so it could not see the sf package or the objects loaded in your live session, which is why your hand-run chunks worked. It also runs chunks from top to bottom, so the chunk that reads and transforms the data has to come before the area chunk. I added library(sf) and moved the read chunk first; the area calculation is unchanged.

)

turns.user: Pull the 150 hp cutoff in this report out into one variable called min_hp, set in a chunk at the top, so changing that single line updates everything in the report, including the sentence.

steps.document:
---
title: "Powerful cars"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
min_hp <- 150
```

```{r}
fast <- subset(mtcars, hp > min_hp)
nrow(fast)
```

Cars above `r min_hp` hp averaged `r round(mean(fast$mpg), 1)` mpg.

```{r}
boxplot(mpg ~ cyl, data = fast)
```

reference.answer: The cutoff is now set once in min_hp in the first chunk. The filter, the sentence and the boxplot all follow it.
